payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism in this chemistry. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim. The cell achieved 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. Its chief operational limitation is a 4 °C temperature floor, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
